*.en: death is nothing to us: what dissolves has no more sensation

anchors.work: Letter to Herodotus (from Diogenes Laertius, Book X)
anchors.startsWith: Death is nothing to us; for that which is dissolved is devoid of sensation, and that which is devoid of sensation is nothing to us.

*.fr: la nature se contente de peu et procure aisément ses richesses ; seuls les désirs vains sont insatiables
*.en: nature is content with little and easily provides her riches; only vain desires are insatiable

anchors.work: Letter to Herodotus (from Diogenes Laertius, Book X)
anchors.startsWith: The riches of nature are defined and easily procurable; but vain desires are insatiable.

*.fr: n'est pas impie qui rejette les dieux de la foule, mais qui leur prête les opinions de la foule
*.en: not impious is he who discards the gods of the crowd, but he who lends them the crowd's opinions

anchors.work: Letter to Herodotus (from Diogenes Laertius, Book X)
anchors.startsWith: And that man is not impious who discards the Gods believed in by the many, but he who applies to the Gods the opinions entertained of them by the many.

summary.en: Epicurus’ physics and ethics as transmitted by Diogenes.

*.fr: la justice n'est pas l'intérêt du plus fort ; l'injustice, à la fin, ne rapporte pas plus que la justice
*.en: justice is not the interest of the stronger; injustice, in the end, pays no more than justice

anchors.startsWith: Then, my blessed Thrasymachus, injustice can never be more profitable than justice.

*.fr: la vérité ne se décrète pas : qui aime la vérité en chaque chose est ami de la sagesse, non de l'opinion
*.en: truth is not decreed: whoever loves truth in each thing is a friend of wisdom, not of opinion

anchors.startsWith: But those who love the truth in each thing are to be called lovers of wisdom and not lovers of opinion.

*.fr: ce qui entre tôt dans une jeune âme y demeure : les premiers récits doivent être des modèles, car l'enfant les garde ineffaçables
*.en: what enters a young soul early stays there: the first tales must be models, for the child keeps them indelibly

anchors.startsWith: For a young person cannot judge what is allegorical and what is literal; anything that he receives into his mind at that age is likely to become indelible and unalterable; and therefore it is most important that the tales which the young first hear should be models of virtuous thoughts.

*.fr: le pouvoir n'est légitime qu'à contrecœur : la cité est le mieux gouvernée quand gouverner coûte
*.en: power is legitimate only reluctantly: a city is best governed when governing costs

anchors.startsWith: Whereas the truth is that the State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed, and the State in which they are most eager, the worst.

*.fr: la vertu ne s'achète pas : c'est elle qui donne tout le reste
*.en: virtue is not bought: it is virtue that gives everything else

anchors.startsWith: I tell you that virtue is not given by money, but that from virtue comes money and every other good of man, public as well as private.

*.fr: l'amour est le désir de son propre entier : nous cherchons l'autre comme la part perdue de nous-mêmes
*.en: love is the desire of one's own whole: we seek the other as the lost part of ourselves

anchors.startsWith: And the reason is that human nature was originally one and we were a whole, and the desire and pursuit of the whole is called love.

*.fr: le bonheur n'est pas un état mais une activité de l'âme ; on est heureux en acte, selon l'excellence
*.en: happiness is not a state but an activity of the soul; one is happy in act, according to excellence

anchors.startsWith: And by Human Excellence we mean not that of man’s body but that of his soul; for we call Happiness a working of the Soul.

*.fr: la vertu est un milieu entre deux excès ; dans l'ordre du bien, c'est le sommet, non une moyenne
*.en: virtue is a mean between two extremes; in the order of the good it is the summit, not an average

anchors.startsWith: And so, viewing it in respect of its essence and definition, Virtue is a mean state; but in reference to the chief good and to excellence it is the highest state possible.

*.fr: la justice est la vertu des rapports : seule entre toutes, elle vise directement le bien d'autrui
*.en: justice is the virtue of relations: alone among the virtues, it aims directly at another's good

anchors.startsWith: And for this same reason Justice alone of all the Virtues is thought to be a good to others, because it has immediate relation to some other person, inasmuch as the Just man does what is advantageous to another, either to his ruler or fellow-subject.

*.fr: la morale ne s'apprend pas avant l'usage : d'abord de bonnes habitudes, ensuite des principes
*.en: morals are not learned before practice: first good habits, then principles

anchors.startsWith: Hence the necessity that he should have been well trained in habits, who is to study, with any tolerable chance of profit, the principles of nobleness and justice and moral philosophy generally.

*.fr: la poésie est plus philosophique que l'histoire : elle dit l'universel, l'histoire le particulier
*.en: poetry is more philosophical than history: it speaks the universal, history the particular

anchors.startsWith: Poetry, therefore, is a more philosophical and a higher thing than history: for poetry tends to express the universal, history the particular.

*.fr: la cité n'est pas née pour vivre seulement, mais pour vivre bien : le pouvoir se juge à la fin qu'il sert
*.en: the city was founded not for life alone but for the good life: power is judged by the end it serves

anchors.startsWith: And when many villages so entirely join themselves together as in every respect to form but one society, that society is a city, and contains in itself, if I may so speak, the end and perfection of government: first founded that we might live, but continued that we may live happily.

*.fr: la meilleure forteresse est de n'être pas haï du peuple : les murs tombent, l'affection tient
*.en: the best fortress is not to be hated by the people: walls fall, affection holds

anchors.startsWith: For this reason the best possible fortress is—not to be hated by the people, because, although you may hold the fortresses, yet they will not save you if the people hate you, for there will never be wanting foreigners to assist a people who have taken arms against you.

*.fr: la guerre n'est juste que nécessaire : quand tout espoir repose sur les armes, les armes sont saintes
*.en: war is just only when necessary: when all hope rests on arms, arms are hallowed

anchors.startsWith: With us there is great justice, because that war is just which is necessary, and arms are hallowed when there is no other hope but in them.

*.fr: la vertu ne quitte pas impunément le droit chemin : qui l'abandonne doit entrer dans les voies du mal pour se maintenir
*.en: virtue does not leave the fair path with impunity: whoever abandons it must enter the ways of evil to survive

anchors.work: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
anchors.startsWith: But he who will not keep to the fair path of virtue, must to maintain himself enter this path of evil.

*.fr: la religion se tient en révérence : c'est un lien de l'État, et son mépris est le signe le plus sûr d'une décadence
*.en: religion is held in reverence: it is a bond of the state, and contempt for it is the surest sign of decay

anchors.work: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
anchors.startsWith: Princes and commonwealths that would save themselves from growing corrupted, should before all things keep uncorrupted the rites and ceremonies of religion, and always hold them in reverence; since we can have no surer sign of the decay of a province than to see Divine worship held therein in contempt.

*.fr: rien n'est de pire exemple qu'une loi qu'on ne garde pas, surtout quand celui qui la rompt est celui qui l'a faite
*.en: nothing sets a worse example than a law not kept, above all when its breaker is its maker

anchors.work: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
anchors.startsWith: Now, though the wicked life of Appius merited every punishment, still it was impolitic to violate the laws, more particularly a law which had only just been passed; for nothing, I think, is of worse example in a republic, than to make a law and not to keep it; and most of all, when he who breaks is he that made it.

*.fr: les hommes sont liés par les bienfaits qu'ils accordent autant que par ceux qu'ils reçoivent
*.en: men are bound by the benefits they confer as much as by those they receive

anchors.startsWith: For it is the nature of men to be bound by the benefits they confer as much as by those they receive.

*.fr: la mort veille sur toi : tant que tu vis, tant que tu peux, sois bon
*.en: death hangs over you: while you live, while you may, be good

anchors.startsWith: Death hangs over thee: whilst yet thou livest, whilst thou mayest, be good.

*.fr: cessons de disputer sur les signes du bon homme : soyons-le réellement
*.en: let us stop disputing the signs of a good man: let us actually be one

anchors.startsWith: Make it not any longer a matter of dispute or discourse, what are the signs and proprieties of a good man, but really and actually to be such.

*.fr: le vrai bonheur tient à très peu de choses
*.en: true happiness rests on very few things

anchors.startsWith: This thou must ever be mindful of, as of this also, that a man's true happiness doth consist in very few things.

*.fr: souviens-toi du pouvoir que la nature t'a donné : nul ne commande à ton jugement
*.en: remember the power nature gave you: no one commands your judgment

anchors.startsWith: Remember then this thy power that nature hath given thee.

*.fr: rien de ce qui est selon la nature ne peut être un mal
*.en: nothing that is according to nature can be evil

anchors.startsWith: But nothing that is according to nature can be evil.

*.fr: j'accepte ce qui vient des dieux et de leur providence : de là tout dépend
*.en: I accept what comes from the gods and their providence: everything hangs on it

anchors.startsWith: I accept it, with reference unto the Gods, and their providence; the fountain of all things, from which whatsoever comes to pass, doth hang and depend.

*.fr: l'excellence suprême n'est pas de vaincre en toutes batailles, mais de briser la résistance sans combattre
*.en: supreme excellence is not conquering in every battle, but breaking resistance without fighting

anchors.startsWith: Hence to fight and conquer in all your battles is not supreme excellence; supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy’s resistance without fighting.

*.fr: tiens tes soldats comme tes enfants : ils te suivront jusqu'au bout
*.en: hold your soldiers as your children: they will follow you to the end

anchors.startsWith: Regard your soldiers as your children, and they will follow you into the deepest valleys; look on them as your own beloved sons, and they will stand by you even unto death.

*.fr: la discipline sans attachement ne fait que des instruments inutiles
*.en: discipline without attachment makes only useless instruments

anchors.startsWith: If soldiers are punished before they have grown attached to you, they will not prove submissive; and, unless submissive, then will be practically useless.

*.fr: interdis les présages : la victoire se calcule et se renseigne, elle ne se devine pas
*.en: ban omens: victory is calculated and informed, never divined

anchors.startsWith: Prohibit the taking of omens, and do away with superstitious doubts.

*.fr: comme l'eau, l'armée épouse le terrain : la victoire suit les circonstances
*.en: like water, an army takes the shape of the ground: victory follows circumstance

anchors.startsWith: Water shapes its course according to the nature of the ground over which it flows; the soldier works out his victory in relation to the foe whom he is facing.

*.fr: la durée épuise : aucun pays n'a profité d'une guerre prolongée
*.en: duration exhausts: no country has profited from prolonged warfare

anchors.startsWith: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.
